structured_output.world_model: W5 (contrarian), after E048. Rebuild noise: the build sets cudnn.benchmark=True, and I think most compiled convs still call cuDNN, which re-picks its algorithm in every fresh process. Pinning Inductor's cache therefore can't make builds bit-identical; only turning benchmark off or forcing deterministic algorithms can, at some time cost. I expect this rebuild spread, not seed-set difficulty, to explain most of the 0.750–0.754 readings of the same commit. Filter wd is inert (Muon renormalizes filters and applies no wd), so every wd effect runs through the SGD groups. Freezes are nearly free only with an annealed LR and only late; annealing group 2 from 70% repeats E037's early-freeze cliff on the biggest block. The stem's max-pool carries accuracy (anti-aliasing and border handling), so a stride-2 conv trades about 0.5 s/pp, worse than the epoch dial (about 1.5 s/pp). Steps, not pixels, carry early accuracy. Selection and step trims all land at about the dial rate.

forecasts.reason: Inductor cache pinning can't pin cuDNN benchmark's per-process algorithm choice, so rebuilds won't be bit-identical; the no-cudagraphs arm also costs over 0.5% in time.
Removing the max-pool (and the border row/column with padding 0) loses accuracy faster than the time saving is worth: about 0.5 s/pp vs the dial's ~1.5.
Selection plus top-up nets about -5 steps and should land on the dial's rate, inside noise.
Annealing group 2 from 70% starves the biggest block during the 32 px phase, like E037's early-freeze cliff.

cruxes: Do the compiled step graphs send convolutions to cuDNN (chosen by cudnn.benchmark) or to Triton templates? If cuDNN, cache pinning can't remove the rebuild spread.
Does the stem's max-pool carry accuracy (anti-aliasing and border handling) beyond its time cost?
Is group 2's late learning at 32 px, from 70% to 90% of steps, needed for accuracy, or only its final 10%?
